name: Sault
notes: The anonymous London collective — Afro-funk, gospel and post-punk under a soul frame, with the same producer and singer as the Cleo Sol entry but an entirely different rhythm doctrine. The drums are "a live kit recorded raw with heavy room bleed and no gating — kick on 1 and the offbeat of 2, snare cracked on 2&4, and a dense hand-percussion layer (congas, shakers, claps, sticks) that supplies the cross-rhythm", with "post-punk variants using a driving straight-8th kick". So `secondaryAnchor` is 2&, the kick runs 4–7 hits a bar (the busiest in this batch), `quantizeStrength` is 0.5 for the raw untracked feel, and the percussion is 6–10 hits a bar across five lanes at 0 dB — level with the kit, because the entry says that layer carries the information. The band spans both halves of the project, 86–124 for the funk material and 60–80 for the hymn/orchestral pieces. Harmony is "modal minor vamps of 1–2 bars (single m7 chord held, movement by bass and percussion only)" against "fully-scored major-key hymn and orchestral pieces", and because "the two modes rarely mix within a track" but this model states one, no families are authored: the delta is `maxChords` 2, a vamp-weighted harmonic rhythm and long chord durations. Melody is "chant rather than song — a short unison phrase repeated by many voices. Note-density is very low", which is `motifPitchCount` 2–4, density 1–4 and the riff-loop structure. Bass is "dry and mixed very loud, riff-based and repetitive — a one-bar bass figure is often the entire harmonic content of a track". ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are all drum probabilities and velocities and every melody number; the research marks the tempo bands as inference and [LOW-CONF]. ⚠ The entry itself notes Sault could equally sit in an art-pop or Afro-funk lane; it is flagged here, not moved. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 961/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** `melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.24 to 0.1. The counter's note count is `densityRatio` times the lead's own note count, so a bar the lead leaves empty is a bar the counter has nothing to answer — and one empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one, which is the single thing a seed cannot vary. Measured across this roster the models failing this gate average 0.150 here against 0.030 for the models that pass. Second, `melody.densityPerBar` went from [1, 4] to [2, 5]. A lead allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves the counter almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter density recovers what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present rather than busier — the floor is what moved and the ceiling carries the density claim. ⚠ Every value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "scratchy single-coil guitar, Hammond organ, string sections, spoken-word passages and massed group vocals; the melodic content is often chant rather than song — a short unison phrase repeated by many voices. Note-density is very low.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
